_note: Args used for Jay Peak's trace pass with the trailmap-trace workflow (9 readers, 71 trails: every trail that is not a named glade or a park; the map draws no lines, so every overlay is a trace). Paths were a scratch dir; sourceImage was a lossless PNG of the same render as public/maps/jay-peak.jpg; all_labels.txt lists every label from the PDF text (name | difficulty | centre | kind).
resort: Jay Peak Resort, Vermont, 2025-26 winter map (painted; no drawn trail lines)
legend: This map draws NO trail lines: each trail is a painted open cut (white / light-blue snow between painted trees), named by black text with a white halo and a difficulty symbol printed just before the name (green circle = easiest, blue square = more difficult, black diamond = most difficult; this map has no double diamonds). There are NO line pieces (the polylines file is empty and the tiles are plain zoomed crops): trace every trail yourself, as source-px points along the open snow its label names, pieces []. Red lines with red text are lifts (Aerial Tram, Flyer Express Quad, Metro Quad, Taxi Quad, Bonaventure Quad, Jet Triple Chair, Village Double Chair, moving carpets). Pink/magenta dashed lines are UPHILL TRAVEL ROUTES, not trails (they often run up a trail's cut; do not follow one past where the trail goes). Yellow dashed = ski area boundary; orange dashed = area of gravest concern. Green dot-grid shading = slow zone. Orange pills and orange-dotted areas = terrain parks. Thick red-pink bands at the lower right = cross-country and snowshoe trails (not ski trails). A trail printed more than once runs through all of its labels. Glades are painted as trees with no open cut: if a trail's label sits in trees with no open snow to follow, write traced [] and start the note with 'NO CUT'. The top-right SIDE VIEW inset and the MOUNTAIN STATS panel are not part of the main map: do not trace in them. Every trail label printed on the map, to tell whose cut is whose: work/jay-peak/all_labels.txt
